evidence: rebar.toml:11: `# Requires the \`nava-rebar[agents]\` extra + a model API key (e.g. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY).`

The new `[llm]` table at rebar.toml:154-160 names only `bedrock:` ids, so the default path uses AWS credentials, not ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an assertion to test_documented_opt_out_returns_resolution_to_anthropic that `LLMConfig.from_env(repo_root=str(_REPO)).model` resolves to an `anthropic:` id under the opt-out overlay (mirror of test_clean_checkout_resolves_the_bare_cfg_model_to_bedrock_too), and byte-pin the anthropic overlay's `[llm] model` scalar.
evidence: test_documented_opt_out_returns_resolution_to_anthropic sets REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE at the anthropic overlay then asserts only `resolved == _class_models(_ANTHROPIC_TOML)` and `target.split(':',1)[0] == 'anthropic'` per class (lines 170-180) — no assertion on `LLMConfig.from_env(repo_root=_REPO).model`.

The diff's whole justification for adding `[llm] model` to rebar.toml is that cfg.model is a SECOND path the class table cannot reach (rebar.toml comment: '`[llm] model` IS SET AS WELL AS THE CLASSES... a SECOND resolution path the class table cannot reach'); test_clean_checkout_resolves_the_bare_cfg_model_to_bedrock_too pins this only for the DEFAULT direction (line 76-92).

config.py:340-351 `_read_llm_file_table` deep-merges the pointer over discovered per key, so cfg.model under opt-out depends on the anthropic overlay carrying its own `[llm] model` scalar; test_project_default_ids_are_byte_equal_to_the_bedrock_overlay byte-pins only the BEDROCK overlay scalar (lines 150-155), nothing pins the anthropic overlay's scalar.

If anthropic.toml's `[llm] model` (line 22) were dropped/drifted, a Bedrock-less contributor taking the documented opt-out would have cfg.model fall back through discovered rebar.toml to `bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8`, silently defeating the opt-out for every cfg.model-resolving op — a concrete regression this suite cannot detect.
advisory.finding: The opt-out test asserts only class-table resolution returns to Anthropic; it does not assert `cfg.model` (the second resolution path) also returns to Anthropic under the opt-out, leaving the mitigation half-verified for the exact contributor it targets.
scenarios: A contributor without Bedrock access sets REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE=anthropic.toml; an op resolving cfg.model (not naming a class) still dispatches to Bedrock and fails on missing AWS credentials.
A future edit removes/renames the anthropic overlay's `[llm] model` scalar; the class-only opt-out test stays green while cfg.model silently leaks back to the Bedrock default.
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_documented_opt_out_returns_resolution_to_anthropic, after setting REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE, add: `model = LLMConfig.from_env(repo_root=str(_REPO)).model; assert model.split(':', 1)[0] == 'anthropic'`. Optionally extend the byte-equal pin test to also assert anthropic.toml carries an `[llm] model` scalar.
